meta.title: How residential construction and renovation projects run: US (NY, CA, CT), England (London), Ireland (Dublin), Canada (Ontario, BC), Mexico (CDMX)

method_values.page: the figure was read on the page itself (WebFetch, or text pulled from a downloaded PDF)
method_values.search-summary: the figure came from a search engine's summary of the page; the page itself was not opened (usually 403) and the figure has not been checked against it

meta.rule: Figures are never invented. Where nothing published was found, the value is null and a note says so. Cost-guide figures (Fixr, HomeGuide, Angi) are aggregator estimates, not measured market data, and should be shown as estimates.

fee_full_service_residential_pct_of_cons.note: Widely attributed to AIA guidance. AIA itself publishes no fee schedule (antitrust), so treat this as the trade's rule of thumb.

fee_renovation_pct.note: Renovations carry higher percentage fees because existing conditions add work. From an architects' marketing page, not AIA.

fee_basis_note.value: AIA B101-2017 ties a percentage fee to the owner's budget at signing rather than to final construction cost.

phase_split_pct_of_fee.note: Bidding/negotiation is usually about 5% and is folded into the bands. These are trade conventions, not AIA-published numbers.

stages_1_to_4_share_of_fee_pct.note: Most London homeowners commission RIBA Stages 1–4 only (through Building Regulations drawings) and run the build themselves.

official_fee_scale.note: RIBA has published no mandatory fee scale since its scales were withdrawn on competition grounds. Percentages above are market observations.

example_stage_split_pct_of_fee.note: Example split for a renovation and extension, reported as following RIAI stage structure.

official_fee_scale.note: The RIAI publishes no mandatory fee scale. Irish competition law ended recommended scales.

fee_residential_pct.note: Market range. OAA defers to the RAIC fee guide (2019), whose percentage charts we could not open; the RAIC guide PDF link returned 404.

raic_guide_residential_chart_pct.note: RAIC 'A Guide to Determining Appropriate Fees for the Services of an Architect' (2019) has percentage charts by category and cost. We could not open the chart (404 at https://www.aanb.org/uploads/bylaw/52/file/translations/103/RAIC_Guide_to_Determining_Fees_2019_Eng.pdf).

single_family_house_new_construction_pct.note: AIBC Tariff of Fees, 4th ed., Category 8(i) Custom/Individual Single Family House, net % for basic architectural services. Excludes GST, engineering and reimbursables. The table was read from PDF text whose column layout was scrambled, so the column assignment should be checked. 'Last monitored February 3, 2009'. AIBC has since withdrawn mandatory tariffs, so this is historical guidance.

single_family_house_renovation_pct.note: Same table, renovations column. The same scrambled-layout caveat applies.

arancel_formula.value: H = CO x FS x FR / 100 (fees = construction cost x surface factor x regional factor / 100)
arancel_formula.note: Federation of Colleges of Architects (FCARM) arancel. We did not find the CAM-SAM arancel's own tables online.

fee_per_m2_mxn_proyecto_ejecutivo_cdmx_w.note: Said to run 20–40% above other Mexican cities.

stages_covered: Proyecto ejecutivo (structural, electrical, hydro-sanitary, gas, finishes, catálogo de conceptos)

hourly_usd.note: Aggregator figures. The ASID fee survey itself was not reachable.

ffe_markup_pct.note: Cost-plus markup on furniture, fixtures and equipment.

UK_IE_CA_MX.note: Not researched to source standard: no BIID, Irish, Canadian or Mexican interior designer fee data was gathered.

UK_recommendation.note: Checkatrade recommends at least three quotes. Most US and UK consumer guidance says the same.

NY_AG.note: The NY Attorney General says to 'look at multiple contractors' and compare quoted prices, with no number given.

US_platform_lead_sharing.note: Angi shares a homeowner's lead with 3–8 contractors. This is how the platform works, not a survey of how many bids homeowners actually get.

measured_average_bids_obtained.note: No published survey of how many bids homeowners actually obtain was found.

academic_highest_minus_lowest_pct_of_awa.note: Design-build / best-value public projects, not residential remodels. 80% of projects fell between 7% and 55%.

academic_bid_std_dev_pct.note: Average standard deviation of bids, construction auctions. Ballesteros-Pérez et al., J. Constr. Eng. Manage. 147(8) 04021096 (2021), showed σ depends mostly on how many bids an auction receives. The 11.6% figure appeared in a search summary and was not seen in the abstract.

academic_low_bid_vs_engineer_estimate.note: Average ratio of low bid to engineer's estimate. Public works.

residential_anecdote_example_usd.note: A contractor's blog example of three bids for one remodel (high is 53% above low). Anecdote, not data.

Angi_HomeAdvisor_Checkatrade_published_s.note: None of these platforms publishes the spread between bids for the same job.

California.cap: lesser of $1,000 or 10% of contract price
California.progress_payments: contractor may neither request nor accept payment exceeding the value of work performed or material delivered
California.quote: the downpayment shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) or 10 percent of the contract amount, whichever amount is less.

rules: Written contract required for home improvement over $500

Payments received before substantial completion go into a NY bank escrow/trust account within 5 business days, and the customer is told where within 10 business days (Lien Law §71-a(4)). The alternative is a bond or contract of indemnity within 10 business days.
Three business days to cancel unconditionally
Progress payment schedule must bear a 'reasonable relationship' to the work done
Final payment withheld until completion and inspections
New_York_State.statute: NY Gen. Bus. Law §§770-776; Lien Law §71-a
New_York_State.note: No percentage cap on the deposit.

rules: Written contract signed and dated by both parties, with the contractor's HIC registration number
Notice of the customer's right to cancel until midnight of the third business day (Saturday counts)
Payments refunded within 10 days of cancellation
Connecticut.note: A search summary claimed a one-third deposit cap under CGS §20-429. The DCP page does not say so and the statute text could not be opened (403 / certificate error), so the claim is unverified.

England.note: No statutory cap. Checkatrade guidance: be cautious above 10%.

Ireland.note: No statutory deposit cap was found. Not researched further.

rules: Written agreement required for contracts over $50
10-day cooling-off period when signed at the customer's home (direct agreement), with refund within 15 days
Final price may not exceed the estimate by more than 10% without the customer's written consent
Changes in writing and signed by both parties
Ontario.note: The 10% deposit figure is provincial guidance, not law.

BC.note: No deposit cap found. Not researched further.

Mexico.note: The 30% anticipo ceiling and the 100% anticipo guarantee come from public-works law (LOPSRM) and do not bind private home renovations. They are the reference figures Mexican contracts commonly borrow.

US_Houzz_2026_study_2025_projects.note: Houzz does not publish the size of the overrun.

US_Houzz_2020_study_2019_projects.designer_quote: Buffer an additional 25% ... Eighty percent of the time you are going to open up [the walls] and run into something (designer opinion, not data)

US_Clever_2024_poll.note: The 78% 'overall' sits oddly beside 53% and 42% for the two subgroups. Prefer the subgroup figures.

change_order_frequency_and_size.note: No reliable published residential figure for how often change orders occur or what they add. Construction-software blogs cite 8–14% and 10–30% of contract value with no traceable study behind them, so they are left out. NAHB publishes no such survey that we could find.

markup_on_change_orders_pct.note: A '15% overhead and profit' convention is widely cited without a source.

US_new_home_build_time_Census_SOC_2025.note: New construction, not renovation. Useful as baseline durations.

average_lateness_weeks.note: No survey publishes the average size of a residential renovation's delay in weeks.

weather.method_note: Contracts set a baseline of weather days from NOAA history (days with >0.10 in. precipitation), and delays beyond it are usually excusable but non-compensable: more time, no more money.

NYC_DOB.period: First four months of Fiscal 2026 (Jul–Oct 2025) vs same period FY2025

Los_Angeles_LADBS.official_text: The plans are reviewed and then returned within weeks depending on workload.
options: Express permit (no plan check, issued immediately)
Los_Angeles_LADBS.note: LADBS publishes no turnaround average. Consultants quote 15–30 business days, which is unverified.

London_actual_elapsed_2025.sample: 21,331 London householder decisions in 2025 (Searchland data, analysed with AI help by an architecture firm)
London_actual_elapsed_2025.note: The official 92–93% counts 'agreed extensions' as on time. This dataset measures raw elapsed time. Both are true.

London_demolition_notice.note: Building Act 1984 s.80. The council may serve a s.81 counter-notice with conditions.

Dublin_planning.note: The '5 weeks / decision after FI' wording comes from DCC's timelines page via search. A search summary said two weeks after FI, but the statutory figure is 4 weeks. Unverified, needs checking. Council medians come from archa.ie's analysis, not official statistics.

Ireland_commencement_notice.note: Required for new buildings, material alterations, extensions and material changes of use. Lodged on the BCMS.

Ontario_statutory.note: The clock runs only on a complete application. Toronto's 3-business-day Express Service is a goal, not law.

Toronto_actual_elapsed.note: Toronto publishes no measured average. Contractor sites claim 6–12 weeks to permit in hand, which is unverified.

Vancouver.note: City press release (June 2026) via search. The page returned 403.

manifestacion_tipo_A.scope: Single-family dwelling up to 120 m² built, 2 levels, 5.5 m height, spans ≤4 m, lot frontage ≥6 m

manifestacion_tipo_B.scope: Up to 5,000 m² or 3 levels (per search summary)
manifestacion_tipo_B.note: The 30–60-day practical figure is from a trade magazine, unverified.

licencia_especial_demolicion.DRO_required_if: ground floor >60 m² or an upper room >16 m²

first_time_failure_rate_overall.note: No jurisdiction in scope publishes a first-time inspection failure rate by trade or overall. A search summary attributed a '65% pass first time' figure to the UK Building Safety Regulator, but no BSR document could be found behind it, so it was rejected. NAR: 24% of buyers of new-built homes said the home 'did not pass the first inspection'. That counts private buyer inspections, not code inspections.

NYC.reinspection_condition: for reinspections made necessary by a failure to correct a condition or respond to a request for corrective action
NYC.incomplete_inspection_fee_status: proposed/adopted rule, 2026: inspector arrives and the work is not ready or not accessible

NYC_audit_failure_rate_professional_cert.note: Plan audits of professionally certified jobs, not field inspections.

Los_Angeles.note: LAMC §91.107 permits a reinspection fee when work is not ready or corrections are not made, and points to LAMC §98.0412 for the rates. We did not get the dollar amount.

Toronto.note: Toronto has no flat re-inspection fee on its fee page. Extra inspection time is billed at the hourly rate.

London_IE_Vancouver_CDMX_reinspection_fe.note: Not found. In England, local-authority building control charges are set by each council.

pool_removal_fixr_usd.note: Fixr's example is a 12x24 ft fiberglass shell.

NYC.rule: A full demolition needs a DOB demolition permit and an ACP-5 (asbestos assessment, building free of ACM) before sign-off. Removing structural members, bearing walls, floors or exterior walls is filed as an alteration (partial demolition). The PW1 must state whether abatement is required, and an ACP-5 or ACP-21 is needed before DOB permits issue for affected areas.

Los_Angeles_pool.rule: Pool demolition needs an LADBS demolition permit plus grading for backfill. Fill compacted to at least 90% relative compaction (ASTM D1557), tested by an approved soils agency, with a compaction report and Certificate of Compliance. A soils report may be required.

England.rule: Building Act 1984 s.80 notice to the council at least 6 weeks before demolition (small buildings and internal work are exempt). Demolishing a dwelling may also need planning prior approval or permission. The detail was not verified.

Ireland.rule: Planning permission is required to demolish a habitable house, a building in a terrace, or a building abutting another in separate ownership. Partial demolition to make way for an exempt extension, and demolition of outbuildings in the curtilage (not abutting another owner's building), are exempt.

Ontario.rule: Building Code Act s.8 requires a demolition permit for any building over 10 m² (farm buildings excepted).

CDMX.rule: Licencia de Construcción Especial (demolición), with a DRO or Corresponsable when the ground floor is over 60 m². See 4_delays_permits_weather.CDMX.

non_US_demolition_costs.note: Not researched. Only US figures were found.

7_rooms_and_finishes_US.note: All US national cost-guide estimates (Fixr, January 2025 updates unless noted). None for the UK, Ireland, Canada or Mexico.

soundproofing_general.example: 150 sq ft room: soundproof windows and door plus extra insulation is about $2,000

recording_rehearsal_studio_room_within_r.note: Studio-builder blogs and forums, not a cost guide. Treat as indicative only.

California.rule: Down payment ≤ lesser of $1,000 or 10%. Each later payment may not exceed the value of work performed or material delivered.

New_York.rule: Payment schedule must bear a 'reasonable relationship' to work done. Pre-completion payments held in escrow (or bonded). Final payment held until completion and inspections.

Ontario.holdback_release: after lien rights expire, 60 days after the contract is published or deemed complete; payable from day 60 to day 74 if no lien is registered
Ontario.annual_holdback_release: mandatory for contracts longer than one year, from January 1, 2026

England.release: half at practical completion, half at the end of the defects period
England.note: Contract practice (JCT etc.), not statute. A homeowner on a small job often has no retention clause at all.

Ireland.release: half at practical completion (RIAI clause 35), half at the end of the defects period or the certificate of making good defects

Mexico.note: Public works (LOPSRM). Private renovations follow no statute, but the estimaciones system (periodic billing against measured progress that amortises the anticipo) is the common model.

US_typical_private_schedule.note: No published survey of milestone splits (for example 10/30/30/20/10) for US residential renovation was found. Only contractor marketing, which is left out.

gaps: No in-scope jurisdiction publishes a first-time inspection failure rate.
LADBS and London/Dublin/Vancouver/CDMX re-inspection fee amounts were not obtained.
No reliable published frequency or size for residential change orders. No average overrun % (Houzz gives only the share over budget). No average lateness in weeks.
No published spread between residential bids for the same job. The only figures are from academic public-works and design-build studies.
No published average of how many bids homeowners actually obtain.
RAIC 2019 fee charts were not reached (404). The AIBC tariff figures come from scrambled PDF text and are historical (2009).
No CAM-SAM arancel tables were found online. Mexico figures come from FCARM-based secondary sources.
Interior designer fees were found only for the US.
Demolition, room and finish costs were found only for the US.
Measured Toronto and LA permit times are unpublished. Statutory or target figures only.
Connecticut's alleged one-third deposit cap is unverified.
